auditor: analytical-auditor (Sonnet, high effort), blind: claim + data paths only, no code, no author reasoning
verdict: partly supported (all numbers reproduce; the causal-sounding conclusion over-reaches)

reproduced.S1-S4_rows: 576 drives / 117 days each, identical rows to S0 (no missing in any block column)
reproduced.eligibility: 2 ens_outlier_v2 true, 12 NaN (kept, NaN is not true); 606 -> 576 after required non-nulls

mismatches: none; max abs diff < 0.001 on every slope and bound, drive/day counts equal

vif_partial_r2.S2: VIF 1.81, R2(months|block+T+I)=0.448; partial R2 of months on y 0.037
vif_partial_r2.S4: VIF 1.83, R2 0.453; partial R2 on y 0.030

alt_variance.wild_cluster_bootstrap_t: Rademacher, null-imposed, 4000, seed 42: p S0 0.0003, S2 0.0013, S4 0.0083

method_concerns: HIGH: window is only 5.1 months (May-Oct 2026); monthly means of the outcome are non-monotonic (21.4, 23.1, 24.3, 22.4, 21.7, 24.5 mV). Time is confounded with season, usage and logger setting; T_pack and peak_I enter only linearly. The slope is a within-window association, not a degradation rate.

HIGH: the S0 slope is not stable: cutoff refits give +0.40, -0.35, +0.16, with CIs covering 0 in all three. Full-sample significance rests on the October data. The pre-registered decision tests only the full-sample slope.

HIGH (logic): proxy adjustment cannot rule out a time-correlated timing confound. Proxies are noisy per-drive summaries (error-in-variables), so adjustment is partial; i_dt_q50 drifts -0.087 s/month, cur_age_p95 correlates -0.51 with months, so the logger-timing change is real and time-correlated. The slope stays stable or rises after adjustment (S2 +34 %), which fits a time-correlated residual confound as well as a genuine trend. Stability under adjustment is weak evidence only.

MED: leakage / bad control. n_loaded, i_abs_*, soc_med, cur_age_p95, chg_share are computed on the same loaded pairs that define the outcome (a p95 depends on support size); they may be mediators / outcome-derived. S3/S4 adjustment is therefore not clean; S1/S2 timing columns are less affected. The S3 result (slope barely changes) is uninformative.

MED: S4 has 15 regressors with 117 clusters. CR1 CIs are about the same as CR3 and wild bootstrap, so CR1 is adequate. S2/S4 are 2x wider (SE 0.21 vs 0.13); the S4 lower bound 0.164 (CR3 0.122) is near zero.

MED: the decision rule ('above half of S0, lower bound > 0') is a low bar. It is satisfied by a slope that moves up and has a wide CI. It is not a TOST or equivalence test and does not show the proxies are exhausted.

LOW: clustering by calendar day is right; no row-level resampling; no cross-validation involved. 4 specifications plus 3 cutoffs plus drift are not multiplicity-adjusted, but the decision uses a conjunction, so no inflation risk for it. Only T and peak_I are unstandardised; the months slope is unaffected by scaling.
language_concerns: 'not explained by the tested proxies' is acceptable as a literal statement; do not extend to 'real degradation', 'not a logger artefact' or 'physical trend'.

State the 5.1-month window, the non-monotonic monthly means, the sign-unstable cutoffs and that the slope is an association (estimated), not a measured degradation rate; 'not excluded' not 'excluded' for logger-timing confounding.
Do not describe S3/S4 as independent controls since they share the outcome's loaded pairs.
